description: Helm registry authentication module allows you to login helm registry login and logout helm registry logout from a Helm registry.

parameters.name: binary_path
parameters.description: The path of a helm binary to use.

parameters.name: ca_file
parameters.description: Path to the CA certificate SSL file for verify registry server certificate.

parameters.name: cert_file
parameters.description: Path to the client certificate SSL file for identify registry client using this certificate file.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Provide a URL for accessing the registry.

parameters.name: insecure
parameters.description: Allow connections to SSL sites without certs. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: key_file
parameters.description: Path to the client key SSL file for identify registry client using this key file.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Desired state of the registry. If set to present attempt to log in to the remote registry server using the URL specified in host. If set to absent attempt to log out from the remote registry server using the URL specified in host. As helm >= 3.18.0 reports successful logout even if the user is not logged in, this module will report a change regardless of the current state. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

examples:
- name: Login to remote registry
  kubernetes.core.helm_registry_auth:
    username: admin
    password: "sample_password"
    host: localhost:5000

- name: Logout from remote registry
  kubernetes.core.helm_registry_auth:
    state: absent
    host: localhost:5000

return_values.name: command
return_values.description: Full helm command executed Returned: always Sample: "/usr/local/bin/helm registry login oci-registry.domain.example --username=admin --password-stdin --insecure"

return_values.name: failed
return_values.description: Indicate if the helm command failed Returned: always Sample: false

return_values.name: stderr
return_values.description: Full helm command stderr, in case you want to display it or examine the event log. Please be note that helm binnary may print messages to stderr even if the command is successful. Returned: always Sample: "Login Succeeded\\n"

return_values.name: stderr_lines
return_values.description: Full helm command stderr, in case you want to display it or examine the event log Returned: always

return_values.name: stdout
return_values.description: Full helm command stdout, in case you want to display it or examine the event log Returned: always

return_values.name: stout_lines
return_values.description: Full helm command stdout, in case you want to display it or examine the event log Returned: always
